findings.explanation: The cited passage gives three gas balance points: all measured units above 70 F (s34), the measured units listed as cold-climate still above 58 F (Figure 79), and only the rating curve of an HSPF-13 unit at 28-40 F. Skipping the measured cold-climate result leaves the viewer thinking a cold-climate model breaks even with gas at 28-40 F, when the cold-climate units actually metered did not get below 58 F.
findings.suggestion: Add the measured cold-climate result before the rating curve, e.g. "Even the measured units listed as cold-climate broke even with gas only above 58 °F; on paper, the rating curve of a then-current cold-climate model brought it down to between 28 and 40 °F."

findings.explanation: The answer says that in "these field tests" the heat pumps kept heating below zero, but s30 reports a field-study site whose compressor did not run below 0 F at all (and the same passage has another that stopped below 4 F). The evidence supports that most units kept heating, not all of them.
findings.suggestion: Narrow it: "In these field tests most units did: they kept heating below zero, with less efficiency and less output, and still got more heat from each unit of electricity than resistance heat."

findings.explanation: The Canadian Climate Institute model compares lifetime costs (equipment and installation as well as energy; see the report's lifetime-cost method), while s34-s36 are running-cost break-even temperatures; "points the same way" presents the two as one measure.
findings.suggestion: Say what it counts: "A cost model for Toronto and Edmonton that counts equipment as well as energy points the same way: ..."

findings.explanation: "Part of that" ties the thermostat to the 25 percent backup time below 0 F in s26, but the passage only says setpoint interference raised the switchover temperature (30-35 F); it attributes none of the below-0 F backup time to it.
findings.suggestion: Detach it from the 25 percent: "Some backup use came from the thermostat: ..."

findings.explanation: "Part is faults" also hangs on the 25 percent in s26, but that figure excludes defrost, which is where both sites engaged the higher stages; only the one site seen doing it in normal heating could contribute.
findings.suggestion: Reword as "Some came from faults: ..." so it does not claim a share of the below-0 F figure.

findings.explanation: The answer to "do they still save money?" is "yes" against propane or electric heat, but the same Minnesota passage that gives the 30-56 percent savings says retrofit paybacks are typically longer than 10 years unless the equipment needs replacing anyway.
findings.suggestion: Add a clause here or in s33: "on running costs, though the Minnesota researchers put retrofit paybacks at over 10 years unless the old system needs replacing."
